intended_object: A proof certificate: a derivation (a term of type `Nominal.NPrf`, which is `Type`-valued) in the object-level first-order proof system. It replays the Metamath/set.mm theorem `elrab`, A ∈ {x ∈ B | φ} ↔ (A ∈ B ∧ ψ), under the hypothesis x = A → (φ ↔ ψ). I inferred this from the docstring ("Checked nominal proof certificate identified upstream as `g_elrab`") and from the definition of `NPrf` in NominalCertificate.lean.
explanation: `NPrf theory atomFormula code` is defined as `∀ rho, Fol.prf theory.fst (Code.lower atomFormula rho code)`, i.e. a family of proof trees. That makes it a `Type`, so derived rules have to be written as `def`s instead of theorems. `gElrab` builds one such proof object. It takes the not-free side conditions (`gNfcv`, `gNfv`), passes them to the more general `gElrabf`, and returns the resulting derivation. It is an internal step in compiling Metamath proofs into the library's Flypitch-based deduction system. It is not the definition of a mathematical notion: it is a formal derivation of a set-theory theorem, kept as data for the library's internal use. So there is no definition to check for faithfulness or generality. If anything, its correctness is the soundness of the encoded statement, and the type checker already guarantees that.
